title: Election Periods and Residence Conditions for Joining a Ridgecrest RxSecure Plan
content:
A Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan election is accepted only under an election period open to the member on the day the plan receives the completed election form.

## The conditions on an accepted election

1. The member's permanent residence recorded on their profile lies in one of the states in the elected plan's region. The states of each plan's region, the membership CMS has approved for it and its published star rating are the ones certified for the plan elected.
2. The enrollment request on file carries an election period code, and where that code names a special election period the request also carries what the plan holds as evidence of the circumstance. Both are read from the enrollment intake record, not from what the member says on the call.

## The election periods

| Election period | When it runs | The coverage it opens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Annual election period | 15 October to 7 December | Coverage beginning the following 1 January |
| Initial enrollment period for Part D | Surrounding the member's first entitlement to Part A or enrollment in Part B | Coverage under the initial period's own terms |
| Loss of creditable drug coverage | Two months from the loss | Coverage elected inside those two months |
| Low-income subsidy quarterly change | Once in each calendar quarter of the first three quarters of the year | A change of drug plan in that quarter |

A member receiving the low-income subsidy may change drug plans once in each calendar quarter of the first three quarters of the year, and that right is checked against the subsidy level CMS supplied rather than against the member's own account of it.

## Where no period is open

Where no election period is open the election is refused, the member is told when the next one opens, and the plan never moves a receipt date to reach a closed period.
